note: Wikidata q-ids only. Centre is Wikidata's point for ancient Delphi (Q75459), not the modern village (Q954068) and not the archaeological site item (Q17652439), which is a separate place in this seed. No entrance is claimed anywhere: no door here has been measured, so every point is a centroid or an area. Delphi is the smallest place in this module and the most spread out, because the sanctuary alone cannot fill a city: the bounds reach Parnassus, the Corycian Cave, Arachova, Galaxidi, Amfissa and the monastery of Hosios Loukas, which is how a family actually spends three days here. Arachova was dropped: as a settlement item it graded D, with Wikipedia 573 m from Wikidata, because a town's coordinate is an arbitrary point inside it rather than a place. That costs this city its only food entry, and no substitute in the area carries a q-id.

places.name: Tholos of Delphi
places.note: The round building itself. The sanctuary of Athena Pronaia that contains it (Q105394638) sits 17 m away, under the separation floor, so the two cannot both ship. The Tholos is the thing a child actually looks at.

places.name: Liakoura, the summit of Parnassus
places.note: Replaces the mountain item (Q105261), which graded D: OpenStreetMap put it 525 m away and Wikipedia 722 m, because all three sources are describing a massif rather than a place. This is Liakoura, the highest peak, which is the point people climb to. Third time this failure has appeared in Greece, after Lycabettus and Juktas.

places.name: Ancient Amfissa
places.note: The archaeological site on the acropolis hill, where the castle stands, rather than the modern town (Q470481) 700 m downhill.

places.name: Monastery of Hosios Loukas
places.note: The monastery (Q844841), not the settlement named after it (Q114490836) 60 m away.
